title: 1982 AHSME Problem 18
statement: In the adjoining figure of a rectangular solid, \(\angle DHG=45^\circ\) and \(\angle FHB=60^\circ.\) Find the cosine of \(\angle BHD.\)

solutions.text:
Let \(H=(0,0,0),\) \(F=(u,0,0),\) \(G=(0,v,0),\) and \(C=(0,0,w).\) Then \(B=(u,0,w)\) and \(D=(0,v,w).\) The \(60^\circ\) condition gives \(w=\sqrt3u,\) while the \(45^\circ\) condition gives \(v=w.\) Hence \[ \begin{aligned} \cos\angle BHD &=\frac{w^2} {\sqrt{u^2+w^2}\sqrt{2w^2}}\\ &=\frac{\sqrt6}{4}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Assign coordinates at \(H\) along the three mutually perpendicular edges
Translate the two given angles into relationships among the three edge lengths, then use a dot product
